actions.reason: RegexTokenizer._encode_ordinary now finds the chunks that are not cached yet with a C-level set difference. When there are at least 16 of them, it UTF-8 encodes them all and joins them with byte 0xff. Valid UTF-8 never contains 0xff, and a merges table that uses 0xff as a token falls back to the old path, so no merge can cross a chunk boundary. It then applies basic._replace_table's increasing-idx str.replace merges once over the joined string, splits it back into chunks and fills the cache. The output is assembled with chain.from_iterable. This gives the same results as apply_merges per chunk (the same argument BasicTokenizer.encode already relies on). Smaller batches, and merges dicts the table rejects, keep the old per-chunk path. Equivalence identical; encode_ir ratio 0.9511.
